TORRANCE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Emmaus Life Sciences, Inc. (OTCQB: EMMA), a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company and leader in the treatment of sickle cell disease, today reported on its financial condition and results of operations as of and for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

Highlights

“Our global net revenues declined for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to the same period in 2025 primarily driven by a 44% decrease in U.S. net revenues as our licensing agreement with NeoImmuneTech Inc. (NIT), became effective on May 15, 2026,” commented Willis Lee, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Emmaus. “The decline was partially offset by a related reduction in our operating expenses. Management believes that the conflict in the Middle East also adversely affected net revenues in the region,” he added.

Financial and Operating Results

Net Revenues. Net revenues for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $1.9 million, compared to $3.4 million in the same period in 2025 driven by lower direct sales of Endari® following the company’s execution of the License Agreement with NIT.

Operating Expenses. Total operating expenses for the three months were $1.9 million compared to $2.4 million in the comparable period in 2025. The decrease was due primarily to decreased expenses attributable to the transfer of our sales force to NIT in connection with the license arrangement.

Income (Loss) From Operations. Loss from operations for the three months was $0.4 million compared to income from operations of $0.7 million in the same period in 2025. The changes were due to the decrease in net revenues, partially offset by lower operating expenses.

Other Expense. The company realized other expense of $4.4 million for the three months compared to $2.2 million in the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily due to change in fair value of conversion features derivative based upon an increase in the company’s stock price.

Net Loss. For the three months, the company realized a net loss of $4.7 million, or $0.07 basic loss per share based on approximately 70.2 million weighted-average common shares, compared to net loss of $2.1 million, or $0.03 basic loss per share based on approximately 63.9 million weighted-average common shares in the comparable period in 2025. The increase in net loss was attributable primarily to the decrease in net revenues and increase in other expense.

Liquidity and Capital Resources. At September 30, 2026, the company had cash and cash equivalents of $1.0 million, compared to $2.1 million at December 31, 2025.

About Emmaus Life Sciences

Emmaus Life Sciences, Inc. is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company and leader in the treatment of sickle cell disease. Endari® (L-glutamine oral powder), indicated to reduce the acute complications of sickle cell disease in adults and children 5 years and older, is approved for marketing in the United States, Israel, Kuwait, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Oman and is available on a named patient or early access basis in France, the Netherlands, and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where Emmaus’ application for marketing authorization is awaiting final action by the Saudi Food & Drug Authority. For more information, please visit www.emmausmedical.com.

About Endari® (prescription grade L-glutamine oral powder)

Endari®, Emmaus’ prescription grade L-glutamine oral powder, was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in July 2017 for treating sickle cell disease in adult and pediatric patients five years of age and older.

Indication

Endari® is indicated to reduce the acute complications of sickle cell disease in adult and pediatric patients five years of age and older.

Important Safety Information

The most common adverse reactions (incidence >10 percent) in clinical studies were constipation, nausea, headache, abdominal pain, cough, pain in extremities, back pain, and chest pain.

Adverse reactions leading to treatment discontinuation included one case each of hypersplenism, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, burning sensation, and hot flash.

The safety and efficacy of Endari® in pediatric patients with sickle cell disease younger than five years of age has not been established.

For more information, please see full Prescribing Information of Endari® at: www.ENDARIrx.com/PI.

About Sickle Cell Disease

There are approximately 100,000 people living with sickle cell disease (SCD) in the United States and millions more globally. The sickle gene is found in every ethnic group, not just among those of African descent; and in the United States an estimated 1-in-365 African Americans and 1-in-16,300 Hispanic Americans are born with SCD.1 The genetic mutation responsible for SCD causes an individual's red blood cells to distort into a "C" or a sickle shape, reducing their ability to transport oxygen throughout the body. These sickled red blood cells break down rapidly, become very sticky, and develop a propensity to clump together, which causes them to become stuck and cause damage within blood vessels. The result is reduced blood flow to distal organs, which leads to physical symptoms of incapacitating pain, tissue and organ damage, and early death.2

1Source: Data & Statistics on Sickle Cell Disease – National Center on Birth Defects and Developmental Disabilities, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, December 2020.

2Source: Committee on Addressing Sickle Cell Disease – A Strategic Plan and Blueprint for Action -- National Academy of Sciences Press, 2020.

JLL is recognized for transforming facility management through an integrated Workplace Management platform, digital innovation, and sector-focused execution that strengthens operational resilience and business performance.

SAN ANTONIO, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As facility management continues to evolve from a largely operational function into a strategic contributor to workplace performance and enterprise resilience, JLL is demonstrating how an integrated approach can create measurable value for organizations across complex environments. Frost & Sullivan recognizes JLL with the 2026 North American Competitive Strategy Leadership Recognition in Facility Management for its ability to combine strategic transformation, digital capabilities, and sector expertise to strengthen its competitive position and deliver integrated facility management (IFM) solutions across the region.

Frost & Sullivan evaluates companies through a rigorous benchmarking process across two core dimensions: strategy effectiveness and strategy execution. JLL excelled in both, demonstrating its ability to align strategic initiatives with evolving market demands while executing them with consistency, scale, and measurable impact. "JLL is a recognized leader in IFM and workplace solutions across North America. Its competitive position is built on a clear strategic progression: redefining Facility Management through the Workplace Management platform, aligning its operating structure to support integrated delivery, and scaling digital and sector-specific capabilities across the United States and Canada. This approach enables JLL to serve commercial office, financial services, life sciences, technology, industrial and advanced manufacturing, data centers, healthcare, and government clients while linking facility operations more directly to business performance," said Janice Wung, Industry Principal, Homes & Buildings, Frost & Sullivan.

JLL's strategic approach centers on its Workplace Management platform, which brings together facilities management, technical services, sustainable operations, safety, sourcing and procurement, workplace experience, and technology-enabled delivery under a single operating structure. The platform supports greater standardization, governance, and scalability across multi-site portfolios while maintaining flexibility for sector-specific requirements.

Digital innovation further differentiates JLL's approach to facility management. Technologies, including Corrigo, JLL Smart Building Platform, Azara, and JLL Falcon AI, support work order and asset management, predictive maintenance, energy optimization, workplace analytics, and portfolio-level performance visibility. These capabilities enable clients to move beyond reactive facility operations toward more proactive, data-driven decision-making.

"We are honored Frost & Sullivan is recognizing JLL's work in facilities management," said Chris Fernandez, Americas Head of Workplace Management at JLL. "At its core, facilities management is about creating environments where people can do their best work while ensuring the buildings they depend on operate safely, reliably and efficiently every day. FM has evolved far beyond maintaining physical assets. Today, it sits at the intersection of workplace experience, operational resilience and business performance. This award reflects the dedication of our teams across North America who help clients care for both their buildings and the people inside them, ensuring workplaces support productivity, collaboration and long-term success."

Frost & Sullivan's recognition comes while broader changes are underway across the facility management industry. JLL's recent Global State of Facilities Management Report 2026 reveals that half of occupiers already view FM as a significant source of competitive advantage, with that figure projected to rise to more than four in five organizations by 2030. Meanwhile, 45% of occupiers are scaling AI across FM operations while nearly 70% have experienced disruptions from skilled labor shortages and technical skills gaps. These converging trends are accelerating demand for integrated workplace management strategies that combine operational expertise, technology and workforce capabilities to support business performance and resilience.

JLL has also demonstrated its ability to translate strategy into execution across complex, high-value environments. In 2025, the company secured integrated facilities management for WestJet's 1.9 million-square-foot portfolio spanning its headquarters and 17 Canadian airport locations, along with the facility maintenance and operations mandate for the $9.5 billion JFK New Terminal One project. For a global tech manufacturer, JLL moved the company's U.S. portfolio from reactive repairs to proactive IFM, saving nearly $1 million on HVAC costs in its first eight months and achieving 4% overall savings in the first year. JLL has also partnered with a Fortune 100 semiconductor company to build a digital FM strategy aimed at cost savings and operational excellence. Together, these engagements show JLL's ability to scale integrated facility management across demanding environments where reliability, compliance, operational resilience, and risk management are critical.

The company's competitive position is further strengthened by integrating energy management, decarbonization initiatives, ESG reporting, workplace experience, and space-utilization analysis into its FM delivery model, JLL addresses the increasingly interconnected priorities of corporate real estate, sustainability, HR, and business leaders.

Frost & Sullivan commends JLL for establishing a differentiated approach to facility management that connects operational performance with broader business outcomes. Through its combination of proprietary technology, advisory-led delivery, sector expertise, and customer-focused execution, JLL is helping shape the future of FM across North America.

Each year, Frost & Sullivan presents the Competitive Strategy Leadership recognition to a company that demonstrates outstanding strategy development and implementation, resulting in measurable improvements in market share, customer satisfaction, and competitive positioning. The recognition highlights forward-thinking organizations that are reshaping their industries through innovation and growth excellence.

Frost & Sullivan Best Practices Recognition

Frost & Sullivan's Best Practices Recognitions honor companies across regional and global markets that exhibit exceptional achievement and consistent excellence in areas such as leadership, technological innovation, customer experience, and strategic product development. Each recognition is the result of a rigorous analytical process in which Frost & Sullivan industry experts benchmark performance through comprehensive interviews, deep-dive analysis, and extensive secondary research. The goal is to identify true best-in-class organizations that are driving transformative growth and setting new industry standards.

JLL (NYSE:JLL) is a leading global commercial real estate services and investment management company with annual revenue of $26.1 billion, operations in over 80 countries and a global workforce of more than 112,000 as of September 30, 2026. For over 200 years, clients have trusted JLL, a Fortune 500® company, to help them confidently buy, build, occupy, manage and invest across a variety of industries and property types, including office, industrial, hotel, multi-family, retail and data center properties. Highlights

  • Joint Development and Commercialisation Agreement signed with UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd., part of UNITEX Group, a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications, combining development and manufacturing capabilities in China with an established customer network spanning more than 100 countries.
  • Initial focus on graphene enhanced carbon fibre prepreg, with plans to expand into thermoplastics, resin concentrates, coatings and elastomers.
  • Agreement combines First Graphene's formulation and dispersion expertise with UNITEX's manufacturing and innovation capabilities, and established international supply network.
  • Provides First Graphene with a pathway into China's composites manufacturing and innovation sector and access to wider international markets, helping to accelerate the development, scale-up and global commercialisation of graphene-enhanced materials across a broad range of applications.

Sydney, Australia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - First Graphene Limited (ASX: FGR) (FSE: M11) (OTCQB: FGPHF) ("First Graphene" or "the Company") is pleased to announce it has entered into a Joint Development and Commercialisation Agreement ("the Agreement") with UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd. ("UNITEX"), establishing a strategic collaboration to develop and commercialise graphene enhanced carbon fibre composites and other advanced materials.

The Agreement represents a further step in First Graphene's strategy to commercialise its graphene technologies through strategic development and manufacturing partnerships. The collaboration draws on UNITEX's material development, engineering and manufacturing capabilities in China, providing First Graphene with a pathway into China's significant composites manufacturing sector and the international markets it supplies.

Headquartered in Ningbo, China's Zhejiang province, UNITEX is a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications. Built on its manufacturing capabilities in China, the group combines material development, application engineering and industrial supply chain integration to translate material technologies into commercially viable products and solutions.

With an established customer network spanning more than 100 countries, UNITEX serves industries including automotive, aerospace, semiconductors, energy, marine, construction and sporting goods.

Its capabilities extend from customised material development and engineering support to industrial-scale manufacturing and global supply, providing a foundation for the international commercialisation of jointly developed materials.

The collaboration will combine First Graphene's expertise in graphene selection, formulation and dispersion with UNITEX's materials engineering, manufacturing infrastructure and established supply chain capabilities.

Development and commercialisation program

The initial development program will focus on graphene enhanced carbon fibre prepreg, building on First Graphene's internal research and development activities, which demonstrated improvements in strength and barrier properties through incorporation of graphene into carbon fibre composites.

Where the results justify further development, the parties intend to progress successful formulations through customer validation, manufacturing scale-up and commercialisation, subject to the agreement of applicable commercial terms. The Agreement term is for three years and is cancellable by either party with three months notice.

Beyond carbon fibre prepreg, the collaboration is expected to explore opportunities across thermoplastics, resin concentrates, coatings, elastomers and other advanced materials, broadening the potential applications and commercial reach of First Graphene's graphene technologies.

The Agreement provides First Graphene with an opportunity to leverage UNITEX's material development, engineering and manufacturing capabilities, together with its established international customer network, to accelerate the development and industrialisation of graphene enhanced materials and bring commercially viable products to global markets.

First Graphene Managing Director and CEO, Michael Bell, said:

"Carbon fibre and advanced composites represent an increasingly important growth opportunity for First Graphene, as manufacturers seek innovative ways to improve material performance and deliver greater value to customers.

Our internal development work has demonstrated the potential of graphene to enhance the strength and barrier properties of carbon fibre composites. The next step is translating technical advances into commercially scalable products through partnerships with established manufacturers.

UNITEX brings extensive expertise in materials development, engineering and manufacturing, alongside an established international customer network. This collaboration provides FGR with a strategic pathway into China's composites manufacturing sector and expand its commercial reach across global markets.

Importantly, the opportunity extends well beyond carbon fibre. By combining our respective technical and manufacturing capabilities, we see significant potential to develop graphene-enhanced thermoplastics, coatings and other advanced materials across industrial applications.

This agreement is another important step in our strategy to move graphene innovation from development into commercial markets and expand First Graphene's international presence."

About UNITEX

UNITEX Composite (Ningbo) Co., Ltd., established in 2017 and headquartered in Ningbo, China, is part of UNITEX Group, a global materials technology group specialising in advanced composites and integrated material solutions for a wide range of applications. Built on its manufacturing capabilities in China and the integration of China's comprehensive industrial supply chain, UNITEX brings together material development, application engineering and industrialisation to deliver customised solutions for global customers. The group serves customers in more than 100 countries, supporting a broad range of industries from material development through to commercial production and international supply.

The Company is a leading supplier of graphitic materials and product formulations with a specific commercial focus on large, high-growth global markets including cement and concrete; composites and plastics; coatings, adhesives, sealants and elastomers (CASE); and energy storage applications.

One of the key outcomes these advanced materials offer is the reduction of carbon dioxide emissions, whether directly through a reduction in output of these harmful greenhouse gases or lower energy usage requirements in manufacturing, or indirectly due to enhanced performance characteristics and extending the usable life of products.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Battery Mineral Resources Corp. (TSXV: BMR) (OTCQB: BTRMF) ("Battery" or "BMR" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr. Frikkie Kruger as Chief Financial Officer of the Company, effective December 1, 2026.

Mr. Kruger, based in Massachusetts, is a Chartered Accountant (South Africa) and a member of the South African Institute of Chartered Accountants with 20 years of progressive finance leadership in the mining and resources sector, with a particular focus on copper. He has held senior finance roles in South Africa, Zambia, the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Middle East, South America and the United Kingdom, working with companies listed on the London, Johannesburg and Santiago stock exchanges.

Mr. Kruger was most recently Group Financial Manager at Moxico Resources PLC, which operates the Mimbula copper mine on the Zambian Copperbelt. He previously served as Chief Financial Officer of Bayete Energy Resources and as Senior Financial Reporting Manager at Enaex Africa. He has supported mining businesses through both the development and operating stages and has built finance functions from start-up. His expertise includes IFRS and U.S. GAAP reporting, multi-entity consolidation, multi-currency treasury, C1-C3 and all-in sustaining cost (AISC) modelling, payable metal calculations and SOX-aligned internal controls.

Laz Nikeas, Chief Executive of BMR, stated, "We are very pleased to welcome Frikkie to the Company. His copper-focused finance and public market experience will be a strong addition to our team."

Mr. Kruger added, "I am delighted to join Battery Mineral Resources at such an important stage for the Company and the Punitaqui Mining Complex. I look forward to working with Laz, the Board and the broader team to strengthen BMR's financial foundation, reinforce disciplined capital management and support the Company's growth strategy."

The Company also announces that it has granted 500,000 restricted share units ("RSUs") to Mr. Kruger pursuant to the Company's restricted share unit plan (the "Plan"). The RSUs will vest in three equal annual instalments commencing on the first anniversary of the date of grant and are subject to the terms and conditions of the Plan and the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange.

About Battery Mineral Resources Corp.

Battery Mineral Resources operates the Punitaqui Mining Complex, a historic copper, gold, and silver-producing mine in the Coquimbo region of Chile. The Company's portfolio also includes 100%-owned ESI Energy Services Inc. and North American mineral exploration assets. The Company is focused on providing shareholders with accretive exposure to copper and the global trend of electrification while targeting growth through cash flow, exploration and acquisitions in favorable mining jurisdictions. Ottawa, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Enablence Technologies Inc. (TSXV: ENA) ("Enablence" or the "Company"), a leading supplier of planar lightwave circuit (PLC) optical chips for datacom, telecommunications, artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced vision applications, today announced it will host a conference call and release financial results for its first quarter of fiscal 2027 ended September 30, 2026, after the market closes on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

Management will host a live conference call that day at 2:00 pm PT / 5:00 pm ET to discuss the company's results and guidance.

A live webcast of the conference call can be accessed from the company's investor relations website at https://www.enablence.com/investors. Following the call, a replay of the webcast will also be available on the investor relations website.

About Enablence Technologies Inc.
Enablence is a publicly traded company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (TSXV: ENA) that designs, markets and sells optical chips and sub systems, primarily in the form of planar lightwave circuits (PLC), on silicon-based chips for datacom, telecom, automotive and artificial intelligence (AI) applications. Enablence products serve a global customer base, primarily focused today on data center and other rapidly growing end markets. Enablence also works with customers that have emerging market uses for its technology, including medical devices, automotive LiDAR, and virtual and augmented reality headsets. In select strategic circumstances, the Company also uses its proprietary, non-captive fabrication plant in Fremont, California to manufacture chips designed by third party customers. BETHESDA, Md.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Walker & Dunlop, Inc. announced today that it has arranged $270,000,000 in refinancing for The Greyson, a 28-story, 622-unit, Class A mixed-use residential tower developed by Nasser Freres in the heart of Jersey City's Journal Square neighborhood. The financing marks a significant milestone for the development, supporting its transition from construction to stabilized operations and positioning the property for long-term success.

The Greyson. Photo credits: Nasser Freres

Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory served as exclusive advisor to Nasser Freres, arranging a floating-rate, interest-only bridge loan from affiliates of Apollo. The transaction was arranged by Keith Kurland, Aaron Appel, Adam Schwartz, Jonathan Schwartz, Jordan Casella, Christopher de Raet, and Jack Krentzman.

"Journal Square has undergone a remarkable transformation, and The Greyson exemplifies the caliber of development attracting investment to the neighborhood,” said Kurland, senior managing director of Capital Markets and co-head of Institutional Advisory at Walker & Dunlop. "With its exceptional location, extensive amenities, and proximity to Manhattan, the property is well-positioned to capitalize on the area’s continued growth. We’re pleased to have worked with Nasser Freres and Apollo to execute this transaction.”

Located at 25 Cottage Street, The Greyson encompasses 424,328 rentable square feet, including 389,328 square feet of residential and 35,000 square feet of commercial space. The property features a collection of studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences with unobstructed views of the Jersey City skyline. Designed to deliver an elevated residential experience, The Greyson offers an extensive suite of amenities, including an art gallery, children's playroom, screening room, gaming lounge, virtual reality and sports room, coffee bar, fitness center, speakeasy, and private event space. Ground-floor retail space leased to a wine bar further enhances the property’s appeal while contributing to Journal Square’s growing dining and entertainment scene.

"From the outset, our vision for The Greyson was to create something truly distinctive, a property that would help shape the next chapter of residential living in Journal Square while contributing meaningfully to the neighborhood’s continued transformation,” said Michael Sokoloff, partner at Nasser Freres. "We’ve been intentional about every aspect of this development, from its architecture and design to the amenities and experiences we’re bringing to residents. We’re incredibly proud of what we’ve built and believe The Greyson will set a new standard for the neighborhood for years to come. This refinancing marks an exciting next chapter as we shift our focus to the property’s long-term success and we appreciate Walker & Dunlop’s advisory.”

Situated along the newly opened Homestead commercial corridor, the property is less than a five-minute walk from the Journal Square Transportation Center, offering direct PATH access to Lower and Midtown Manhattan in approximately 10 and 20 minutes, respectively. Journal Square has emerged as one of the New York metropolitan area's fastest-growing rental submarkets, driven by demand for transit-oriented housing and rental rates that remain comparatively affordable to those along the Jersey City Waterfront and in Manhattan.

In the first half of 2026, Walker & Dunlop’s Capital Markets team sourced over $13.9 billion from non-Agency capital providers, including nearly $9.6 billion for multifamily properties. This vast experience has made them a top advisor on all asset classes for many of the industry’s top developers, owners, and operators. To learn more about Walker & Dunlop’s broad financing options, visit our website.

Walker & Dunlop (NYSE: WD) is one of the largest commercial real estate finance and advisory services firms in the United States and internationally. Our ideas and capital create communities where people live, work, shop, and play. Our innovative people, breadth of our brand, and our technological capabilities make us one of the most insightful and client-focused firms in the commercial real estate industry.

Key Terms

floating-ratefinancial
A floating-rate is an interest rate on a loan, bond or other debt that moves up or down over time based on a regularly published reference number, so the payments change as market rates change. For investors, that means income and interest costs track current market conditions—like a thermostat that adjusts with room temperature—offering protection when rates rise but adding uncertainty about future cash flow.
interest-onlyfinancial
A loan or payment plan where the borrower pays only the interest for a set period while the original loan amount (the principal) stays unchanged; after that period payments typically rise to cover principal or a lump-sum principal payment is due. For investors this matters because interest-only structures change cash flows and risk: they can boost short-term income but increase the chance of payment shock or default later, similar to renting a car without paying down the purchase cost until the final bill arrives.
bridge loanfinancial
A bridge loan is a short-term loan used to quickly provide funds until a larger, long-term financing option is in place. It acts like a temporary bridge, helping individuals or businesses cover immediate expenses or complete transactions without delay. For investors, it’s important because it offers quick access to cash but often comes with higher costs and short repayment periods.

RICHMOND, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Everforth, Inc. (NYSE: EFOR) (“Everforth”) announced today that it has withdrawn its previously proposed offering of $500 million in aggregate principal amount of senior notes due 2031 as a result of market conditions.

The proposed transaction was opportunistic to refinance the Company’s existing 4.625% senior notes well in advance of their May 2028 maturity. While Everforth had meaningful investor interest, the Company made the strategic decision to withdraw the offering as the terms do not reflect the strength of its business.

Everforth’s strong free cash flow and liquidity position provide the Company with significant financial flexibility. Everforth remains committed to using its free cash flow to reduce debt and further strengthen the balance sheet. The Company will continue to evaluate a range of financing alternatives to address the 2028 maturity.

TAICHUNG, Taiwan, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd (the “Company”) today announced that on November 13, 2026, its Indonesian operating subsidiary, PT AGCC AITECH INDONESIA (the “Indonesian Subsidiary”), entered into two definitive contracts with separate contractors for the mechanical, electrical and plumbing (“MEP”) works for Phase 1B of the Company’s planned AGCC-JKT01 data center in West Java, Indonesia (the “Data Center”): an equipment supply agreement for the procurement and supply of MEP equipment (the “Supply Contract”) and an installation works contract for the installation of the MEP equipment and systems (the “Installation Contract” and, together with the Supply Contract, the “Contracts”). The Contracts provide for delivery of the equipment and completion of the installation works during 2027, in accordance with the milestones set out in the Contracts. Each Contract provides for liquidated damages for delay, subject to a cap, and for a defects notification period following taking-over of the installed works. The Indonesian Subsidiary may terminate either Contract for convenience on notice, subject to payment for work performed and other costs reasonably incurred by the relevant contractor.

The Contracts relate to the construction of the Data Center and do not themselves generate revenue. Completion of Phase 1B and commencement of operations at the Data Center remain subject to, among other things, performance by the contractors engaged by the Company and its subsidiaries (the “Group”), completion of related construction and power supply works, availability of funding and applicable regulatory approvals. TORONTO, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Talisker Resources Ltd. ("Talisker" or the "Company") (TSX: TSK, OTCQX: TSKFF) is pleased to provide an update on the continued advancement of its ore sorter facility (“Sorting Facility”) at the Company’s 100% owned Bralorne Gold Project (“Bralorne”).   Construction and engineering activities have continued to advance according to plan, with several major project milestones already completed and a number of critical work programs now entering the execution phase.

Key Highlights:

  • Initial operation of the Sorting Facility is targeted for Q2 2027, with full commissioning expected in July-August 2027.
  • Electrical infrastructure is completed and targeted for commissioning by the end of November 2026, providing power for the future operation of the Sorting Facility.
  • Phase 1 earthworks associated with the electrical infrastructure required to support the Sorting Facility were successfully completed in September.
  • Phase 2 earthworks and concrete foundation construction is planned to commence late November 2026, following removal of legacy infrastructure.
  • Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) of the TOMRA XRT Sorter is scheduled for early December 2026, with the ore sorter expected to arrive in Canada in January 2027.
  • Major long-lead equipment procurement is substantially complete, with the jaw crusher, cone crusher, vibrating screen plant received in Bralorne in October, conveyors, compressors, and buildings being delivered in phases starting December 2026.
  • Construction and mechanical installation activities are planned throughout Q1 2027, supported by completion of detailed engineering and issuance of the remaining construction tender packages in December 2026.

Phase 1 earthworks associated with the electrical infrastructure required to support the Sorter Facility was successfully completed in September. The electrical infrastructure has been procured and installed, with final commissioning scheduled for the end of November 2026. The Mustang Mine power generation and distribution system consists of two 1.5 MW diesel generators, providing a total installed generation capacity of 3 MW at 600 V. The generators can operate in parallel or independently, providing redundancy and backup capability.

Power for the underground mining operations is stepped up to 4.16 kV through a 3,200 kVA transformer and distributed to underground substations that will supply mining equipment.

Surface power distribution is installed and ready to serve the sorting and crushing facilities, as well as supporting all other surface infrastructure requirements. The electrical system incorporates protective switchgear, circuit breakers, ground-fault monitoring, and neutral grounding resistors to ensure safe and reliable operation during the next phase of project development. The power plant and distribution network have also been designed to accommodate the future addition of a third generator unit, allowing for straightforward expansion of site power capacity as operational requirements increase.

As part of the ore sorter site preparation activities, a legacy electrical system located within the planned Sorting Facility footprint has been safely dismantled and removed, clearing part of the area for Phase 2 Earthworks construction. In parallel, the Company has completed construction of a new tension-fabric steel frame heavy-duty mechanic shop and is currently transitioning operations from the legacy shop. Demolition of the former shop is expected to be completed in November, fully opening the sorter site for Phase 2 Earthworks before the end of November.

The Phase 2 Earthworks and concrete contractor is scheduled to mobilize to site in November, marking the beginning of a major construction phase. This work will include cut-and-fill activities, foundation preparation, and pre-cast concrete installation within the area previously occupied by the legacy electrical infrastructure and mechanic shop.

Detailed engineering for the project continues to progress well. Issue-for-Tender packages covering the remaining construction components including equipment installation, electrical and mechanical are expected to be completed in December 2026, positioning the project for construction execution through the first half of 2027.

Procurement efforts have been highly successful, with all major equipment purchased. Equipment is either in manufacturing or pending delivery. A proactive approach to early procurement has significantly de-risked the project schedule and supports the Company's objective of maintaining construction momentum throughout the coming months.

A key milestone will occur during the second week of December when the Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) is conducted for the TOMRA XRT sorter. Following successful testing, the ore sorter is expected to arrive in Canada in January 2027.

The crushing circuit has also reached an important milestone, with all major crushing equipment including the jaw crusher, cone crusher, and vibrating screen plant, now delivered and in Bralorne. The compressor system required to support sorter operations is expected to ship for delivery in January 2027.

Building fabrication remains on track, with the manufacturing of two tension-fabric steel frame buildings completed and ready for shipment. The remaining two buildings are expected to be completed and shipped in January 2027.

Engineering and fabrication of the conveyor systems is progressing well. Initial conveyor deliveries are expected to begin arriving on site in mid-December, with additional conveyors being manufactured and shipped in priority sequence throughout the first quarter of 2027.

Taken together, these achievements represent substantial progress toward delivery of one of the Company's most important infrastructure projects. The project continues to transition from planning into full-scale execution with detailed engineering, procurement, and construction activities advancing simultaneously.

The Sorting Facility remains on schedule for operational readiness in the second quarter of 2027, with full commissioning anticipated during July-August 2027. Pre-commissioning activities will involve sorting existing stockpile inventory, providing an opportunity to validate system performance ahead of full scale operations. Once operational, the Sorting Facility will process run-of-mine material and is expected to enhance gold grades while eliminating dilution prior to trucking and shipping, improve operating efficiencies, reduce transportation costs, and strengthen project economics.

Terry Harbort, President and CEO, stated, "We are very pleased with the progress being made on the Sorting Facility. With key infrastructure completed, major equipment secured, and construction activities continuing to ramp up, the project remains on schedule for operational readiness in Q2 2027. This Sorting Facility represents an important milestone for Bralorne and will play a significant role in improving operational efficiency and supporting the Company's long-term growth objectives."


Figure 1: Aerial view of the Mustang Mine site with a rendered overlay of the sorting facility. The recently completed machine shop and the Mustang Mine power generation systems are shown to scale in their actual locations. The Sorting Facility rendering is provided for conceptual illustration only and may not be to scale. The product sorting process flow is indicated by the gold arrows, with major sorting equipment labelled in sequence from 1 through 4.


Figure 2: 3D rendering of the Sorting Facility. The product sorting process flow is indicated by the gold arrows, with major sorting equipment labelled in sequence. Run-of-mine material is loaded into the jaw crusher (1) via the loading ramp and conveyed to the triple-deck screening plant (2). Screened material is then transported to the TOMRA XRT sorter (3), where gold-bearing material is separated from waste rock. The sorted product is conveyed to the cone crusher (4) before being stockpiled within a covered tension-fabric storage building. Waste reject material is conveyed to a separate waste stockpile.


Figure 3: Mustang Mine and Sorting Facility Power Generation System will power all Mustang Operations including the ore sorter, with 100% redundancy.


Figure 4: Left, the Mustang Mine and Sorter Facility power generation system in the foreground, and the new tension-fabric steel frame mechanic shop in the centre background. Right, the new Mustang Mine Mechanic shop.


Figure 5: The Jaw Crusher, Cone Crusher, vibrating screen plant and all crushing circuit equipment frames arrived in Bralorne in October. Installation of the crushing circuit is expected to commence in Q1 2027.

Vancouver, British Columbia and Montreal, Quebec--(Newsfile Corp. - November 18, 2026) - Plurilock Security Inc. (TSXV: PLUR) (OTCQB: PLCKF) ("Plurilock" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that, at the special meeting (the "Meeting") of holders (the "Shareholders") of common shares of Plurilock (each, a "Plurilock Share" and, collectively, the "Plurilock Shares") held on November 18, 2026, Shareholders voted in favour of the special resolution (the "Arrangement Resolution") approving the previously announced plan of arrangement (the "Arrangement") with Quantum eMotion Corp. (NYSE American: QNC) (TSXV: QNC) (FSE: 34Q0) ("QeM" or the "Company"). The Arrangement is being completed pursuant to the terms and conditions of a definitive arrangement agreement between Plurilock and QeM dated September 28, 2026 (the "Arrangement Agreement").

Under the Arrangement, QeM will acquire all of the issued and outstanding Plurilock Shares. Shareholders will receive C$0.084 in cash and 0.0763 of a common share of QeM (each whole common share of QeM, a "QeM Share") in exchange for each Plurilock Share they hold (together, the "Consideration"), implying total consideration of C$0.28 per Plurilock Share. Further, all outstanding options to acquire Plurilock Shares ("Plurilock Options") will be cancelled in exchange for QeM Shares and cash in the same proportions as the Consideration having a value equal to the amount (if any) by which C$0.28 exceeds the applicable exercise price per Plurilock Option. All outstanding restricted share units will vest immediately prior to the effective time of the Arrangement and be settled for the Consideration. All outstanding warrants and convertible debentures of Plurilock will, in accordance with their terms and without further action by the holders thereof, entitle the holders to receive, upon exercise or conversion, the Consideration in lieu of Plurilock Shares.

Shareholders holding a total of 68,226,137 Plurilock Shares were represented in person or by proxy at the Meeting, representing 60.38% of the 112,989,001 issued and outstanding Plurilock Shares entitled to vote as of October 1, 2026, the record date for the Meeting.

The Arrangement required the approval of: (i) at least two-thirds (66⅔%) of the votes cast by Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote at the Meeting; and (ii) a majority of the votes cast by Shareholders present in person or represented by proxy and entitled to vote at the Meeting, excluding Plurilock Shares held by "interested parties" as defined in Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions ("MI 61-101").

At the Meeting, 99.58% of the votes cast by Shareholders (99.54% after excluding Plurilock Shares required to be excluded under MI 61-101) were in favour of the Arrangement Resolution.

The Company will seek a final order (the "Final Order") of the Supreme Court of British Columbia (the "Court") to approve the Arrangement on November 20, 2026. Completion of the Arrangement is subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions for a transaction of this nature, including receipt of the Final Order. Subject to the satisfaction (or waiver) of the closing conditions, it is expected that the Arrangement will be completed shortly after the receipt of the Final Order. Following completion of the Arrangement, it is expected that the Plurilock Shares will be delisted from the TSX Venture Exchange (the "TSXV").

QeM has secured a demand loan of up to C$15,000,000 (the "Loan") from National Bank of Canada (the "Bank") to fund the Arrangement and for general corporate purposes. QeM obtained the Loan because C$15,000,000 of its cash is currently held in an interest-bearing guaranteed investment certificate ("GIC") and will become available upon the GIC's maturity in July 2027. The Loan bears interest at the Bank's Canadian prime rate plus 0.50% per year from the date of disbursement until repaid in full. The Loan is repayable on demand and, in any event, no later than July 31, 2027 (the "Maturity Date"). The Loan is secured by first-ranking security over QeM's deposits and investments.

(NYSE American: QNC) (TSXV: QNC) (FSE: 34Q0) is developing quantum-secure cybersecurity technologies designed to protect digital systems, communications and data in an increasingly complex cyber-threat environment. QeM's technology portfolio combines quantum-generated entropy, quantum-safe cryptography and cybersecurity technologies designed for applications across enterprise, cloud, communications, critical infrastructure and other security-sensitive environments. Plurilock sells cybersecurity solutions and delivers critical IT and cybersecurity services to public- and private-sector organizations. DELTA, British Columbia, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- RecycLiCo Battery Materials Inc. (“RecycLiCo” or the “Company”) (TSX.V: AMY | OTCQB: AMYZF | FSE: ID4), a critical minerals refining and lithium-ion battery upcycling company, is pleased to announce the results of its 2026 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders, held November 17, 2026.

Shareholders representing approximately 31.82% of the Company’s issued and outstanding shares participated in person or by proxy and approved all matters of business before the meeting, including the setting of the number of directors, the election of directors, and the appointment of the auditor.

Richard Sadowsky (Interim CEO), Paul Hildebrand (Chairman), Rod Langtry, Kurt Lageschulte and Rob Chang were each re-elected to serve as directors of the Company until the next annual meeting of shareholders or until their successors are duly elected or appointed.

Richard Sadowsky, Interim CEO of RecycLiCo said, “On behalf of the entire Board and management team, I want to thank our shareholders for their participation and continued engagement. We appreciate the perspectives shared by shareholders at the meeting and remain committed to disciplined execution, responsible research and development, and creating sustainable long-term value as we work to support a secure and resilient domestic supply of critical minerals and metals for North America.”

The shareholders also approved the re-appointment of De Visser Gray LLP as the Company’s auditor until the close of the next annual meeting.

About RecycLiCo 

RecycLiCo Battery Materials Inc. is a critical minerals refining company specializing in the use of advanced hydrometallurgical technologies for processing mined ore and the upcycling of lithium-ion battery materials. RecycLiCo’s processes efficiently recover battery-ready lithium, cobalt, nickel, and manganese from end-of-life batteries and manufacturing scrap, supporting energy storage as well as broader industrial applications. RecycLiCo’s business focus aligns with the global demand for future-ready, responsible supply chains and the growing movement to strengthen domestic sourcing of critical materials.

  • Poster presented today at CTOS 2026 expands on the survival data first reported in the abstract (announced 11 November 2026), which showed a 12-month disease-free survival (DFS) of 81.1% in patients with resectable soft tissue sarcoma.
  • Patients with post-treatment tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) levels above 310 cells/mm² had 95.0% 12-month DFS compared with 64.9% in patients with lower TIL levels.
  • Patients with treatment-related hyalinisation and fibrosis greater than 52% had 93.8% 12-month DFS compared with 71.4% in patients with lower levels.
  • Results build on previously reported strong pathological responses and further support the potential of efti-based combination therapy.

SYDNEY, AUSTRALIA, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Immutep Limited (ASX: IMM; NASDAQ: IMMP) (“Immutep” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel LAG-3 immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune diseases, today announced new data from the investigator-initiated EFTISARC-NEO Phase II study presented at the Connective Tissue Oncology Society (CTOS) 2026 Annual Meeting (Poster number P 448).

The study is evaluating Immutep’s eftilagimod alfa (efti) in combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) and radiotherapy before surgery in patients with high-risk, resectable soft tissue sarcoma. Forty patients were enrolled, and 38 patients underwent surgery and were included in the survival evaluation.

The latest analysis currently shows a disease-free survival (DFS) of 81.1% at 12 months. The current Kaplan-Meier estimate at 18 months is also 81.1%, although this later time point remains immature, and follow-up is ongoing. Among the 38 patients who underwent surgery and were evaluated, eight patients had experienced disease recurrence at the data cut-off (April 30, 2026).

Table 1 – Survival results for soft tissue sarcoma patients from EFTISARC-NEO

OutcomeLatest Analysis
12-month disease-free survival (mature)81.1%
18-month disease-free survival (immature)81.1%
12-month local recurrence-free survival94.1%
12-month distant metastasis-free survival86.2%
Median follow-up19.1 months


In addition, exploratory analyses showed that higher levels of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) and greater hyalinisation and fibrosis after treatment may be associated with better DFS. In particular, patients with post-treatment TIL levels above 310 cells/mm² had 95.0% 12-month DFS compared with 64.9% in patients with lower TIL levels. Patients with treatment-related hyalinisation and fibrosis greater than 52% had 93.8% 12-month DFS compared with 71.4% in patients with lower levels of hyalinisation and fibrosis. The presence of tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) and baseline expression of PD-L1, LAG-3 and TIGIT did not correlate with survival outcomes.

These survival and exploratory findings build on previously reported EFTISARC-NEO results in which the trial met its primary endpoint with a median tumour hyalinisation/fibrosis of 51.5% following neoadjuvant therapy with efti, pembrolizumab and radiotherapy. The new data are consistent with efti's mechanism of action, in which activation of antigen-presenting cells drives a stronger anti-tumour T cell response, and suggest that a stronger immune response in the tumour may be associated with improved patient survival outcomes.

Pawel Sobczuk, MD PhD, one of the Principal Investigators of EFTISARC-NEO, said: “These results are highly encouraging for patients with high-risk soft tissue sarcoma, where recurrence remains a major concern despite surgery and radiotherapy. Disease-free survival of approximately 81% maintained through 12 months and on a preliminary basis also at 18 months is an important observation, and the association between a strong immune response in the tumour and better disease-free survival is particularly compelling. Together with the substantial pathological responses previously reported, the findings reinforce the potential of this novel neoadjuvant approach and provide a strong rationale for continued follow-up and further clinical evaluation.”

Marc Voigt, CEO of Immutep, said: “With the data to date, EFTISARC-NEO is delivering an increasingly coherent and encouraging picture. The marked difference in outcomes between patients with higher and lower post-treatment immune cell infiltration is especially notable and is consistent with efti’s potential to help generate a stronger anti-tumour immune response. We believe these results strengthen the rationale for further potential clinical development in this indication, where patients remain in need of more effective treatment options.”

The poster is available on the Posters & Publications page of Immutep’s website.

Next Steps

Immutep anticipates reporting additional data from EFTISARC-NEO in CY2027.

Subject to regulatory interactions, manufacturing timelines, partnering arrangements and available resources, the Company is preparing to advance efti into a registration-directed clinical trial in neoadjuvant soft tissue sarcoma, targeting initiation in H2 CY2027.

About EFTISARC-NEO

EFTISARC-NEO is an investigator-initiated, open-label Phase II trial evaluating eftilagimod alfa (efti) in combination with KEYTRUDA® (pembrolizumab) and radiotherapy as neoadjuvant treatment for patients with resectable soft tissue sarcoma. The trial is led by the Maria Skłodowska-Curie National Research Institute of Oncology in Warsaw, Poland, and is primarily funded by a grant from the Polish Medical Research Agency, with Immutep supplying efti.

The primary endpoint is pathological response, measured as the percentage of tumour hyalinisation/fibrosis at resection. Secondary endpoints include safety, disease-free survival, local recurrence-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, overall survival, radiological response and health-related quality of life. Forty patients were enrolled, with enrolment completed in January 2025 (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06128863).

About Eftilagimod Alfa (efti)

Eftilagimod alfa (efti) is Immutep’s proprietary soluble LAG-3 protein and MHC Class II agonist that activates antigen-presenting cells through the MHC Class II pathway, engaging both innate and adaptive immunity, including the priming of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and the production of co-stimulatory signals and cytokines. Its favourable safety profile enables combination with anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy. Efti has received Fast Track designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in first-line head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and first-line non-small cell lung cancer, and Orphan Drug Designation in soft tissue sarcoma.

About Immutep

Immutep is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing novel immunotherapies for cancer and autoimmune disease. The Company is a pioneer in the understanding and advancement of therapeutics related to Lymphocyte Activation Gene-3 (LAG-3), and its diversified product portfolio harnesses LAG-3’s ability to stimulate or suppress the immune response. Immutep is dedicated to leveraging its expertise to bring innovative treatment options to patients in need and to maximise value for shareholders. For more information, please visit www.immutep.com.

— A novel EGFR-directed ATTC with a potent pan-KRAS payload designed to overcome resistance and systemic toxicity associated with EGFR/KRAS inhibition —

— Broad-spectrum activity across multiple KRAS mutations, combining inhibition of both ON and OFF states to intercept adaptive resistance —

HONG KONG and SHANGHAI and FLORHAM PARK, N.J., Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HUTCHMED (China) Limited (“HUTCHMED” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq/AIM:​HCM; HKEX:​13) today announces preclinical data for HMPL-A830 presented at the EORTC-NCI-AACR International Conference on Molecular Targets and Cancer Therapeutics, held on November 18–20, 2026, in Barcelona, Spain. HMPL-A830 is a first-in-class Antibody-Targeted Therapy Conjugate (“ATTC”) drug candidate comprises a highly selective and potent KRAS small molecule inhibitor payload conjugated to an anti‑epidermal growth factor receptor (“EGFR”) antibody.

RAS mutations represent one of the most prevalent and well-established drivers in human oncology, driving the progression and aggressive pathology of multiple solid tumors. While recent targeted therapies have validated KRAS (the most dominant RAS isoform) as a viable therapeutic target, significant clinical gaps remain, including safety limitations and disease progression driven by acquired resistance, often mediated by upstream receptor tyrosine kinase upregulation. HMPL-A830 is designed to address this unmet need by delivering a KRAS inhibitor directly to EGFR-expressing tumors, while simultaneously blocking EGFR and KRAS signaling to enhance efficacy, durability, and tolerability.

In vitro profiling demonstrated that its pan-KRAS payload exhibits a dual-action mechanism, simultaneously blocking both KRAS “ON” (GTP-RAF1 binding) and “OFF” (GDP-to-GTP exchange) activities. Potent antiproliferative activity was observed across a broad panel of 55 tumor cell lines harboring diverse KRAS alterations, including G12C, G12D, G12V and G13D mutations, as well as wild-type amplification. HMPL-A830 exhibited high binding affinity and rapid internalization into EGFR-positive cells. It also demonstrated a strong bystander killing effect, effectively eliminating neighboring EGFR-negative tumor cells, while maintaining robust antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) activity.

In mouse models, HMPL-A830 showed dose-dependent and robust antitumor efficacy across various EGFR-positive tumor models harboring KRAS alterations. HMPL-A830 achieved more durable tumor regressions than KRAS G12C inhibitors and outperformed several comparative regimens, including its unconjugated antibody, a pan-RAS inhibitor (administered alone or in combination with cetuximab), and a TROP2-targeted Topo I-inhibitor antibody-drug conjugate. Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) analyses confirmed a stronger and more sustained inhibition of EGFR/KRAS downstream signaling than the naked antibody, alongside a stable drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR) maintained in mouse, monkey, and human plasma.

In September 2026, HUTCHMED Limited (a subsidiary of the Company) entered into an exclusive development and license agreement with a subsidiary of GSK plc (“GSK”), granting the GSK subsidiary worldwide rights excluding Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan to develop and commercialize HMPL-A830. HUTCHMED Limited is responsible for the global Phase I development program of HMPL-A830. The GSK subsidiary will be responsible for all subsequent clinical development and commercialization activities outside of Mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. 

The Phase Ia part of an ongoing global Phase I trial is currently evaluating HMPL-A830 in patients with unresectable, advanced, or metastatic solid tumors (NCT07718581).

About HUTCHMED ATTCs

HUTCHMED’s ATTCs represent a next-generation approach to precision oncology, combining monoclonal antibodies with proprietary small-molecule inhibitor payload platforms to deliver dual mechanisms of action. Unlike traditional cytotoxin-based antibody-drug conjugates, ATTCs combine targeted therapies to achieve synergistic anti-tumor activity and durable responses in preclinical models, outperforming standalone antibody or small-molecule inhibitor components in both efficacy and safety.

Built on over 20 years of targeted therapy expertise, the ATTC platforms enable development of drug candidates across diverse cancer types. By leveraging antibody-guided delivery and tumor-specific payload release, ATTCs improve accessibility to tumors and reduce off-tumor toxicity. This may overcome the on-target, off-tumor toxicity limitations of systemically-delivered small molecule inhibitors, which in turn could ensure safer long-term use and support combinations with chemotherapy and immunotherapy in earlier-line treatments.

About KRAS

RAS mutations represent one of the most prevalent and well-established drivers in human oncology, driving the progression and aggressive pathology of multiple solid tumors. KRAS, the most dominant RAS isoform, is mutated in approximately 44% of colorectal cancer (“CRC”), 34% of lung adenocarcinoma and up to 89% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (“PDAC”) patients.1 KRAS regulates key downstream pathways, including RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT/mTOR, to drive cell differentiation, proliferation, and survival.

While recent targeted therapies have validated KRAS as a viable therapeutic target, significant clinical gaps persist, particularly for patients with non-G12C mutations. Most patients eventually experience disease progression driven by acquired resistance, largely fueled by upstream receptor tyrosine kinase upregulation and secondary KRAS alterations. Beyond mutation coverage, systemic delivery of pan-KRAS and pan-RAS inhibitors is associated with on-target toxicities, such as dermatological toxicity reflecting RAS pathway inhibition in normal tissue. These present challenges for dosing, long-term tolerability, and combination with cytotoxic chemotherapy or immunotherapy backbones that constitute frontline standard-of-care.

About EGFR

EGFR is a widely expressed receptor tyrosine kinase and established driver of tumor cell proliferation, survival, and disease progression across multiple solid tumors, including CRC, PDAC, and non-small cell lung cancer (“NSCLC”). Signaling through EGFR activates the downstream RAS/MAPK and PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathways, positioning the receptor immediately upstream of KRAS. EGFR has also emerged as a key mediator of resistance to KRAS-targeted therapies, particularly in CRC, where adaptive feedback and increased upstream EGFR signaling reactivate the MAPK pathway and limit the depth and durability of KRAS inhibition. Together, these provide a strong rationale for the dual targeting of EGFR and KRAS, not only in CRC but also additional indications such as PDAC and NSCLC.

About HUTCHMED

HUTCHMED (Nasdaq/AIM: HCM; HKEX: 13) is an innovative, commercial-stage, biopharmaceutical company. It is committed to the discovery and global development and commercialization of targeted therapies and immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer and immunological diseases. Since inception it has focused on bringing drug candidates from in-house discovery to patients around the world, with its first four medicines marketed in China, the first of which is also approved around the world including in the US, Europe and Japan.
